description: P1.6 Tauri command/event skeleton + P1.7 secret entry command in tauri-app. Wire AppState (Arc-wrapped subsystems: SessionManager, Db, SecretStore) in state.rs; wire the core-event -> Tauri emit bridge in events.rs (this is where the Phase 0 #[allow(dead_code)] placeholders CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL / forward_core_event get consumed - remove those allows once used); add validated command handlers in commands.rs for the session/persona surface (list/create/rename/set_conversation_tags/delete conversations; list/create/update/delete personas) with argument validation per Section 9.2; and add set_provider_secret(providerId, secret) writing straight to the keystore and returning only a SecretRef. Confirm no command path returns a secret to the webview. Depends on FEAT-002 (SessionManager, SecretStore, CoreEvent). tauri-app is excluded from the workspace and CI-verified via --manifest-path (Phase 0 pattern); it needs crates.io deps so it CANNOT build offline.
steps: Read architecture.md Sections 9.1 (set_provider_secret returns only SecretRef; no command returns a secret), 9.2 (IPC allowlist, capability-scoped permissions, per-command argument validation, no secrets across bridge, event hygiene), 7.3 (core is authoritative, events keep frontend cache in sync). Read the current crates/tauri-app/src/{main.rs,state.rs,events.rs,commands.rs} and capabilities/default.json. Read FEAT-002 findings for the SessionManager/SecretStore/CoreEvent APIs.

AppState (crates/tauri-app/src/state.rs): replace the empty placeholder with fields holding Arc-wrapped subsystems - the SessionManager (over the persistence Db) and the SecretStore. Add path deps on orchestrator-core, persistence, secrets in tauri-app/Cargo.toml (already present as path deps from Phase 0 - confirm). Provide an initializer that opens the SQLite Db (at an app-data path; for a test/dev panel a fixed path is acceptable), runs migrations, constructs the SessionManager and the keyring-backed SecretStore, and returns AppState. Register it via .manage(...) in main.rs.

Event bridge (crates/tauri-app/src/events.rs): wire CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL + forward_core_event to the real orchestrator_core::events::CoreEvent type. Replace the placeholder `payload: ()` with the real CoreEvent, and spawn/connect a task that pumps the core event stream to the frontend via app.emit(CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL, event). REMOVE the two Phase 0 #[allow(dead_code)] attributes now that both items are used. Ensure emitted payloads are display-safe (no secrets) per Section 9.2 event hygiene.

Command handlers (crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs): add #[tauri::command] handlers delegating to SessionManager via AppState: list_conversations, create_conversation, rename_conversation, set_conversation_tags, delete_conversation, list_personas, create_persona, update_persona, delete_persona. Each MUST validate arguments before touching the core per Section 9.2: type/enum-membership checks (e.g. valid PrivacyTag/PermissionMode/ProviderKind), id existence/UUID parse, string bounds (non-empty name, max length), and reject invalid input with a structured error (never partially applied). Keep the existing app_version command. Register every new command in main.rs's tauri::generate_handler!.

P1.7 secret entry command (commands.rs): add set_provider_secret(providerId: String, secret: String) that validates providerId, writes the secret straight to the SecretStore (keyring) via AppState, and returns ONLY a SecretRef (the handle). It MUST NOT return the secret. Audit every command signature to confirm no return type or event payload carries raw key material (Section 9.1/9.2). Add a code comment documenting the no-secret-across-IPC invariant at this command.

Capabilities (crates/tauri-app/capabilities/default.json): grant the webview only the specific commands added (least privilege per Section 9.2). Note from Phase 0: custom commands are authorized by generate_handler! registration, not by capability entries (those gate built-in plugins) - preserve that Phase 0 note; add capability entries only if the project's Tauri v2 setup requires them for custom commands. Do not broaden filesystem/shell/network capabilities.

Frontend IPC wrappers: extend hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts with typed wrappers for each new command (listConversations, createConversation, renameConversation, setConversationTags, deleteConversation, listPersonas, createPersona, updatePersona, deletePersona, setProviderSecret) using the DTO/SecretRef types from src/types/. Update src/ipc/events.ts so CoreEvent is the real union mirrored from orchestrator-core's CoreEvent (replace the `unknown` placeholder) with per-variant discrimination matching the serde tag. Keep vitest green: update or add a minimal vitest test if needed so the frontend suite still passes (mocked invoke), matching the Phase 0 vitest pattern.

Restart-survival acceptance: since tauri dev cannot run in the sandbox (no Tauri CLI, offline), satisfy the 'survives restart' acceptance with an automated test instead - add a tauri-app test (run in CI via --manifest-path) OR an orchestrator-core/persistence integration test that: constructs AppState/SessionManager against a temp SQLite file, creates a conversation and a persona, drops the manager/pool, reopens a fresh Db/SessionManager against the SAME file, and asserts the conversation and persona are still present. Document that the interactive `tauri dev` panel check is deferred to CI/manual since the sandbox has no Tauri CLI.

Author files with LF line endings. Run cargo fmt where possible. tauri-app needs crates.io deps (tauri, sqlx via persistence, keyring via secrets) unreachable offline, so it CANNOT build in the sandbox - do NOT attempt network installs. Ensure the CI workflow already builds+tests+clippies tauri-app via --manifest-path (Phase 0 step); confirm the new commands/state/events are covered. Record in findings that tauri-app build/test is deferred to CI, and that the restart-survival test lives where it can actually run in CI.
acceptance_criteria: AppState holds Arc-wrapped SessionManager + SecretStore, initialized (open Db, run migrations, build subsystems) and registered via .manage() in main.rs.
events.rs wires CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL + forward_core_event to the real CoreEvent type and emits display-safe payloads; the two Phase 0 #[allow(dead_code)] attributes are REMOVED.

commands.rs exposes validated handlers: list/create/rename/set_conversation_tags/delete conversations and list/create/update/delete personas, each validating args (types/enums/ids/bounds) and rejecting invalid input with structured errors; all registered in generate_handler!.
set_provider_secret(providerId, secret) writes to the keystore and returns only a SecretRef; no command return type or event payload carries raw secret material.
frontend ipc/commands.ts + ipc/events.ts are extended with typed wrappers and the real CoreEvent union; vitest suite stays green.
A restart-survival test (runnable in CI) creates a conversation + persona, reopens the DB, and asserts both persist.
Files use LF line endings; tauri-app build/test deferred to CI is documented; CI builds+tests+clippies tauri-app via --manifest-path.
verification: tauri-app requires crates.io deps and CANNOT build offline; primary verification is CI via `cargo build/test/clippy --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml`. Do NOT attempt network installs.

If node_modules were installable this would run `npm run test`; offline it cannot. Confirm the vitest test files are consistent with the Phase 0 pattern; frontend vitest verification is CI-authoritative.
Read commands.rs to confirm every handler validates arguments before calling the core and that set_provider_secret returns a SecretRef (not the secret).
grep the diff to confirm the two #[allow(dead_code)] attributes in events.rs are removed and CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL/forward_core_event are actually used.
Read the restart-survival test to confirm it reopens a fresh Db against the same file and asserts persistence of both a conversation and a persona (not a static assert).
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (P1.6 command/event skeleton + P1.7 secret entry)
- AppState (crates/tauri-app/src/state.rs): replaced the empty placeholder with `Arc<SessionManager>` + `Arc<dyn SecretStore + Send + Sync>` + an `UnboundedSender<CoreEvent>` (the core->frontend event channel sender; the pipeline pushes onto it in Phase 2). Two constructors: `initialize(db_path)` (async: opens the SQLite Db via `Db::open`, runs migrations, builds `SessionManager` + `KeyringSecretStore`, creates the mpsc channel, returns `(AppState, UnboundedReceiver<CoreEvent>)`), and `new(session_manager, secret_store)` for tests (returns the same tuple; used with an in-memory Db + `InMemorySecretStore`). Registered via `.manage(app_state)`.
- Split tauri-app into a lib + thin bin so integration tests can reach the modules (standard Tauri v2 layout). NEW `src/lib.rs` exposes `pub mod commands/events/state`, `DB_FILENAME`, and `run()` (blocks on `AppState::initialize`, `.manage(...)`, a `.setup(...)` hook that spawns the event bridge, and `generate_handler!` with all 11 commands). `src/main.rs` is now just `fn main() { tauri_app::run() }`. The DB path is a fixed relative filename for the Phase 1 dev panel (per-OS app-data dir deferred to a later phase, per architecture.md).
- Event bridge (src/events.rs): wired `CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL` + `forward_core_event` to the REAL `orchestrator_core::CoreEvent` (replaced the Phase 0 `payload: ()`). Added `spawn_core_event_bridge(app, rx)` which drains the core `UnboundedReceiver<CoreEvent>` and calls `forward_core_event(&app, event)` -> `app.emit(CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL, event)` (serde `type`-tagged camelCase, matching the TS union). BOTH Phase 0 `#[allow(dead_code)]` attributes REMOVED; the call chain spawn->forward->CHANNEL is live (grep-verified: 0 `allow(dead_code)` in tauri-app). Emitted payloads are display-safe by construction (CoreEvent carries no secrets); the bridge forwards verbatim and adds nothing.
- Command handlers (src/commands.rs): added validated `#[tauri::command]`s delegating to `AppState.session_manager`: list/create/rename/set_conversation_tags/delete conversations and list/create/update/delete personas. Every handler validates BEFORE touching the core (Section 9.2): UUID parse for ids (`parse_uuid`), non-empty + max-length bounds for names/titles/system prompts (`validate_nonempty`/`validate_opt_len`), bounded tag/tool-server counts, non-empty custom privacy-tag values, and manual-route field checks; enum membership (PrivacyTag/RoutingHint/PermissionMode/ProviderKind) is enforced by serde deserialization of the typed DTOs. Invalid input returns a structured `CommandError { code: InvalidArgument|NotFound|Internal, message }` (Serialize; never partially applied; never echoes secrets). `update_persona` checks existence first and returns NotFound if absent. `app_version` retained. All 11 registered in `generate_handler!`.
- P1.7 set_provider_secret(providerId, secret): validates providerId (non-empty, bounded) and secret (non-empty, <= 8 KiB), writes straight to `AppState.secret_store.store(providerId, secret)`, and returns ONLY the `SecretRef` handle. A prominent NO-SECRET-ACROSS-IPC comment documents the invariant. AUDIT: no command return type or event payload carries raw key material - `SecretStore::resolve` (the single plaintext seam) is NOT exposed as a command (grep-confirmed: `resolve` appears only in comments + the internal-only unit test). SecretRef serializes as the bare handle string.
- Capabilities (capabilities/default.json): preserved + extended the Phase 0 note that Tauri v2 custom commands are authorized by `generate_handler!` registration (now in src/lib.rs), NOT by capability entries (those gate built-in plugins). Still only `core:default`; no fs/shell/network granted. No new entries needed for the custom commands.
- Cargo.toml: confirmed path deps on orchestrator-core/persistence/secrets present; added `tokio` (rt-multi-thread/macros/sync, for `block_on` init + the mpsc channel) and `uuid` (v4/serde) as concrete-literal deps (excluded crate cannot inherit from workspace), plus dev-deps `tempfile` + `tokio` for the integration test.
- Frontend IPC: extended frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts with typed wrappers for all new commands (listConversations, createConversation, renameConversation, setConversationTags, deleteConversation, listPersonas, createPersona, updatePersona, deletePersona, setProviderSecret) using DTO/SecretRef types from src/types; arg names/shapes mirror the Rust handler signatures (create_conversation takes `{ args }`, persona commands take `{ persona }`). events.ts: replaced the `unknown` CoreEvent placeholder with a re-export of the REAL discriminated union from src/types (already mirrored from events.rs in FEAT-002); `onCoreEvent` now yields `Event<CoreEvent>` for full `switch(payload.type)` narrowing. Added frontend/src/ipc/commands.test.ts (vitest, mocked invoke, Phase 0 pattern) asserting each wrapper invokes the right command name/args and that setProviderSecret returns only the handle.
- Restart-survival test (crates/tauri-app/tests/restart_survival.rs): runs in CI via `cargo test --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml`. Opens AppState against a temp SQLite FILE (tempfile), creates a conversation + a persona, DROPS the state/SessionManager/pool (simulating app exit), reopens a FRESH Db/SessionManager against the SAME file, and asserts both the conversation (id + title) and the persona (id + name) are still present. A genuine persistence round-trip, not a static assert. Uses `InMemorySecretStore` so no OS keychain is needed on headless CI.

OFFLINE-VERIFIED (green in sandbox)
- cargo build --workspace (members providers/mcp-client/routing) -> OK; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings -> OK; cargo fmt --all --check -> clean.
- cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check -> clean (ran fmt to normalize).
- cargo verify-project --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml -> {"success":"true"} (manifest parses).
- grep-verified: 0 `#[allow(dead_code)]` remain in tauri-app; CORE_EVENT_CHANNEL/forward_core_event/spawn_core_event_bridge are all used; `resolve` never called from a command.
- All new/modified files confirmed LF.

DEFERRED TO CI (authoritative gate; cannot run offline - IDENTICAL to Phase 0 tauri-app and FEAT-001/002)
- cargo build/test/clippy for tauri-app FAIL OFFLINE ONLY at crates.io dependency resolution (verified: `cargo build --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml` -> HTTP 403 downloading the crates.io index for `serde`/`tauri`). This is a NETWORK failure, NOT a code/compile error. CI (network, ubuntu/macOS/windows) already builds+tests+clippies tauri-app via `--manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml` (existing steps) and runs `tauri build`; the new commands/state/events + the restart_survival integration test are picked up there automatically (tests/ is auto-discovered).
- Frontend vitest/lint/format:check + tsc run in CI (no node_modules offline; npm 403). The new commands.test.ts follows the Phase 0 mocked-invoke pattern and the TS wrappers/union were hand-checked against the Rust signatures and serde attributes.
- Interactive `tauri dev` panel check is deferred to CI/manual (no Tauri CLI in the sandbox); the restart-survival acceptance is satisfied by the automated integration test above instead.

NOTES
- CoreEvent's own `#[allow(dead_code)]` (in orchestrator-core/src/events.rs) was left as-is: its variants are still not all CONSTRUCTED yet (the Phase 2 streaming pipeline constructs message events). The tauri-app bridge FORWARDS CoreEvent generically, which does not construct every variant, so that allow is correctly a Phase 2 concern, not FEAT-003's. FEAT-003 only had to remove the two tauri-app placeholders, which it did.
- Split-crate layout: `tauri_app` is now both a lib (for tests) and a bin; `main.rs` calls `tauri_app::run()`.
